articles.title: Congo mining forum announces $965 million in sector financing
articles.snippet: Congo mining forum announces $965 million in sector financing Kitco
articles.text:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo will receive $965 million in mining-sector investment, organizers announced at the opening of the Makutano Mining Forum in Kinshasa.
Of that total, $700 million is earmarked for financing in the Congolese mining sector, with financial institutions committing to support the sector and its entire value chain.
The remaining $265 million is being provided through the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to support the private sector in the DRC.
The financing will support small and medium-sized enterprises, mining subcontracting, local processing of resources and trade finance.
President Felix Tshisekedi used the opening ceremony to reaffirm the DRC’s aim to move beyond extracting resources to creating added value through local processing, saying this would bring “lasting prosperity for the people.”
(Reporting by Congo newsroom. Editing by Ayen Deng Bior and Mark Potter)
Reuters

articles.text:
Carson Group Adds $944 Million Firm Pinney & Scofield
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:58 AM
Carson Group Adds $944 Million Firm Pinney & Scofield
Pinney & Scofield has joined Carson Group’s integrated advisor channel, expanding Carson’s presence in Greater Boston. The Cambridge, Massachusetts, firm advises on approximately $944 million in assets and will gain access to Carson’s technology, tax and estate planning specialists, and operational support.
The firm began in 1984 as a tax practice founded by Jim Pinney and George Kinder. Dean Scofield joined in 1986, and the practice later shifted toward financial planning and investment management. With the founders retired, the team includes managing partners and wealth advisors John Goddard and Richard Seeley, wealth advisor Mary Evans, and senior relationship and operations manager Ryan McCarthy.
Pinney & Scofield plans to retain its investment models, client fee structure and autonomy. The four-person team chose Carson after evaluating how to expand its resources while keeping advisors’ time focused on clients. MarshBerry advised Pinney & Scofield on the transaction. Carson reports more than $66 billion in assets under management.
KEY QUOTES
“Pinney & Scofield has built something remarkable: nearly $1 billion in assets under management, a loyal multigenerational client base and a deeply personal approach to advice, all with a team of four. John, Richard and their team have been intentional about preserving what makes their firm special while preparing for its future. We’re excited to provide the technology, expertise and infrastructure to help them continue growing while staying focused on the clients and relationships that have made them successful.”
Burt White, CEO Of Carson Group
“We’ve been fortunate to grow almost entirely through referrals, but we reached a point where continuing to build everything ourselves would take time and attention away from what we love most: working with clients.”
John Goddard, Managing Partner And Wealth Advisor At Pinney & Scofield
“I’ve described our expertise as being a mile wide but in some places only a few feet deep. With Carson’s network of expertise and resources, we think we will be a mile wide and a mile deep while preserving the Pinney & Scofield DNA established by our founders. We think it’s a win-win.”
Richard Seeley, Managing Partner And Wealth Advisor At Pinney & Scofield
“Pinney & Scofield is a great example of a successful independent firm making a proactive decision about its future. MarshBerry did an excellent job understanding what mattered most to the team and recognizing the cultural fit with Carson from the outset. We’re excited to build on the strong foundation Pinney & Scofield has established and help position the firm for continued growth.”
Michael Belluomini, Senior Vice President Of Mergers & Acquisitions At Carson Group

Four Startups Raise $515 Million for AI Agent Tools
Funding flows to companies building search, messaging, browsing and data infrastructure that AI agents use to act on the web.
Updated on Nov. 25, 2026 in Artificial Intelligence
Four startups raised a combined $515 million to build infrastructure for AI agents, which increasingly search, text and browse on behalf of users. Exa raised $250 million in May at a $2.2 billion valuation and has passed $100 million in annualized revenue.
Why it matters
Automated systems already account for 57.4% of web requests worldwide, and investors are betting that agent traffic will outpace human activity online. Companies are also adjusting contracts to clarify who is responsible when agents act for a customer.
Exa handles two billion requests a month from more than 200,000 teams, while Linq has processed more than 1 billion messages for customers. Firecrawl's Alexandria library and Parallel Web Systems' search tools are still early, and the stub does not report their usage levels.
The players
Wells Fargo
Wells Fargo is a major U.S. bank that updated its online access agreement to make customers responsible for AI agents acting on their behalf.
Cloudflare
Cloudflare is an internet infrastructure company that launched Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents instead of people.
Andreessen Horowitz
Andreessen Horowitz is a venture capital firm that led Linq's $90 million funding round.
Parag Agrawal
Parag Agrawal is the former CEO of Twitter who launched Parallel Web Systems.
The details
Exa raised $250 million in May, Parallel Web Systems raised $100 million in April, Firecrawl raised $75 million in September, and Linq raised $90 million in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz. Linq lets AI agents text and call people, Cloudflare launched Kitesurf in August as a cloud-hosted browser built for agents rather than people, and Exa said its funding would help it scale to hundreds of thousands of searches per second.
Timeline
April 2026: Parallel Web Systems raised $100 million.
May 2026: Exa raised $250 million at a $2.2 billion valuation.
August 2026: Cloudflare launched Kitesurf for AI agents.
September 2026: Firecrawl raised $75 million.
November 24, 2026: Wells Fargo updated its online access agreement for AI agents.
The Tech Race
Cloudflare's Kitesurf, a cloud-hosted browser built for AI agents rather than people, signals that major infrastructure providers now treat agent traffic as a distinct market. The four funding rounds show rival startups racing to supply the search, messaging and data layers those agents depend on.
Wells Fargo's updated agreement makes customers responsible for any AI agent that acts on their behalf, so people using agents for banking tasks should review the terms before delegating access. As agents begin texting, calling and browsing for users, the choices people make about which tools to trust will shape their daily privacy and convenience.
The takeaway
Agents now act on behalf of their users in ways that carry financial and legal responsibility, so checking how a provider assigns liability is worth the time before granting access. Reviewing those terms early helps users keep control over what their agents do.
Further reading
For more on how these agent tools are reshaping the web, see Artificial Intelligence .

Saudi Startups Raise $338 Million with KAUST Support
November 26, 2026
From quantum computing and cybersecurity to fintech and healthcare, Saudi startups are expanding across diverse tech sectors, benefiting from a research ecosystem aimed at turning scientific innovations into commercial products and attracting new investments.
66 startups within the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) portfolio raised $338 million in funding during the fiscal year spanning from July 2025 to June 2026, achieving a year-on-year growth exceeding 30%, which brings the total funding attracted by portfolio companies to $1.4 billion, while their total valuation stands at $5.7 billion.
The KAUST portfolio includes 282 active startups that have generated cumulative revenues of $1.1 billion, while attracting 90% of their funding from sources outside the university, reflecting the expanding investor base in companies supported by the university’s ecosystem.
KAUST provided about $77 million in funding, while external funding sources included the National Technology Development Program (NTDP), which contributed approximately $33 million.
Pasqal, a company specializing in quantum computing, topped the most prominent funding rounds during the period after raising $200 million, followed by COGNNA, which operates in cybersecurity with a funding of $9.2 million, alongside Aajil, Iyris, and Agellus Tank Robotics.
KAUST portfolio companies are distributed across multiple sectors including artificial intelligence, enterprise software, financial technology, healthcare, agriculture, and advanced technologies, as part of developing companies based on technical innovation and scientific research.
Ian Campbell, Senior Vice President of the National Transformation Institute (NTI) at KAUST, stated that the success of the portfolio companies reflects the environment provided by the Kingdom for the growth and expansion of companies, pointing out the university’s role in helping entrepreneurs turn their innovations into commercial products and transfer them from labs to markets.
In supporting companies, KAUST relies on combining early-stage funding with access to specialized laboratories and facilities, alongside partnerships with The Saudi Awwal Bank (SAB), the National Technology Development Program, the National Industrial Development and Logistics Program (NIDLP), venture capital firms, and private sector partners.
Company support programs include the TAQADAM accelerator, NextEra, ScaleX, the Venture Studio program, and the KAUST Center for the Fourth Industrial Revolution, while the university is working to expand the venture building program aimed at establishing new companies, developing intellectual property, and transforming it into commercial projects linked to the Kingdom’s strategic priorities.

KAUST-Backed Startups Raise $338M in a Year, Up More Than 30%
66 startups in KAUST's portfolio raised $338M between July 2025 and June 2026, lifting the portfolio's total funding to $1.4 billion.
By Abdelrahman Amr 26 November 2026 · 3 min read
Summary
Sixty-six KAUST portfolio startups raised $338 million in the year to June 2026.
That marks growth of more than 30% on the previous year.
The portfolio's cumulative funding has now passed the billion-dollar mark.
Quantum computing company Pasqal led the year with a $200 million round.
Around 90% of the portfolio's funding came from outside the university.
Sixty-six startups in the portfolio of King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) raised $338 million in the financial year that ran from July 2025 to June 2026. That is growth of more than 30% year on year, and it lifts the total funding raised by the university's portfolio companies to $1.4 billion, with a combined value of $5.7 billion.
The numbers come from KAUST's annual assessment of its entrepreneurship portfolio, which covered 282 active startups and drew on data supplied by 83% of them, alongside standard valuation methods. Between them, those 282 companies have generated cumulative revenue of $1.1 billion.
Perhaps the most telling figure is where the money came from. Around 90% of the portfolio's funding was raised from sources outside the university. KAUST itself put in roughly $77 million, while the National Technology Development Program (NTDP) contributed about $33 million among the outside backers.
The biggest round of the period went to Pasqal, the quantum computing company, which raised $200 million. Cybersecurity firm COGNNA followed with $9.2 million, and Aajil, Iyris and Agellus Tank Robotics were also among the notable raises.
The spread of sectors is wide: AI, enterprise software, fintech, healthcare, agriculture and advanced technologies. The portfolio includes iStoria and Faheem in education, Kestrl and EdfaPay in financial services, Cura and Atomica AI in healthcare, Barakah and Aqua Development in food, and TileGreen and Edama in waste management, recycling and resource use.
Ian Campbell, Senior Vice President of KAUST's National Transformation Institute (NTI), said the portfolio's success reflects the environment the Kingdom offers for companies to grow and expand, and pointed to the university's role in helping entrepreneurs turn their innovations into commercial products and move them from the lab to the market.
So how does the support actually work? KAUST pairs early-stage funding with access to its laboratories and specialised facilities, and it works with partners including SAB, the NTDP, the National Industrial Development and Logistics Program (NIDLP), venture capital firms and private-sector partners. articles.title: Alice Huang-Linked Firms Secured $270M In AI Servers In China
articles.snippet: Alice Huang-Linked Firms Secured $270M In AI Servers In China Arise News
articles.text:
09:02, 25th Nov, 2026 by AriseNews
Alice Huang-Linked Firms Secured $270M In AI Servers In China
Global
Chinese records reveal how companies linked to Alice Huang’s family used hundreds of AI servers to secure financing.
">
Follow ARISE News on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google
Follow us on Google
Companies linked to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang raised financing against up to $270 million worth of artificial intelligence servers and computing modules in China, according to records reviewed by Reuters.
The documents, drawn from a Chinese central-bank credit registry, identify up to 764 servers and computing modules, alongside $31 million in networking equipment.
The findings come as US authorities investigate whether Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company formerly controlled by Huang, helped Chinese buyers obtain restricted Nvidia technology.
The US Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on Monday. The company has denied wrongdoing and said Huang left in August 2025.
A major player in the financing arrangements was Century Litong, an Nvidia preferred cloud partner that rents computing servers to customers.
Records show the company entered five equipment-leasing arrangements covering up to 512 servers valued at approximately $200 million between May and December 2024.

Four of the arrangements listed equipment at the Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing centre in Shanghai, a facility developed by gaming company Century Huatong.
Tencent, which holds approximately 10 per cent of Century Huatong, said it never owned or operated the data centre and had no commercial relationship with Megaspeed or its subsidiaries.
The records also link several companies involved in the arrangements to Huang’s sister, Huang Yu, and her husband, Kang Wei. A separate company connected to Huang’s sister pledged 252 AI computing modules as collateral for a $70 million loan in April 2026.
However, the records do not establish that the identified servers contained chips prohibited from export to China or explain how the equipment entered the country.
The dollar figures represent the value of assets covered by financing arrangements, not necessarily new spending or separate purchases.

articles.title: India Startup Funding Tracker: Where Did The $104.4 Million Raised This Week Go?
articles.snippet: India Startup Funding Tracker: Where Did The $104.4 Million Raised This Week Go? Sahyadri Startups
articles.text:
Home › Spotlight › India Startup Funding Tracker: Where Did the $104.4 Million Raised This Week Go?
India Startup Funding Tracker: Where Did the $104.4 Million Raised This Week Go?
Spotlight Posted on November 26, 2026 • Updated November 26, 2026 —by Salil Urunkar
Share
Share on WhatsApp
Share on X
Share on LinkedIn
Share on Telegram
Pune: India Startup Funding reached $104.4 million across 10 funding rounds between 20 and 26 November 2026, but the headline growth figure masks a more concentrated funding environment.
Five transactions accounted for more than 93% of the capital raised, while seed-stage investments contributed just 6.6% of the weekly total.
Join our WhatsApp community Subscribe to our email newsletter
The latest India Startup Funding Tracker by Tracxn and Sahyadri Startups recorded a 46.85% increase in funding compared with the $71.1 million raised in the previous week across 11 rounds.
However, the composition of this week’s investments is more revealing than the increase itself. A single Series C transaction by Bengaluru-based Finnable contributed $43.8 million, accounting for nearly 42% of all capital raised. Without this deal, the weekly funding total would have been approximately $60.6 million.
India Startup Funding: Early-Stage Companies Attract Capital, But Seed Funding Remains Small
The stage-wise distribution reveals an interesting shift in the funding mix.
Stage Funding Share of weekly funding Rounds
Early stage (Series A and B) $53.7M 51.4% 4
Late stage (Series C and above) $43.8M 42% 1
Seed and angel $6.9M 6.6% 5 Source: Tracxn
Early-stage companies attracted the largest share, raising $53.7 million across four Series A and B transactions. This represents 51.4% of the weekly funding.
The continued presence of Series A and B investments is significant for founders building businesses beyond the initial product-development stage.
These companies are typically seeking capital to strengthen their technology, expand operations and move towards larger commercial opportunities.
However, the relatively small seed-stage allocation presents a different picture. Five companies raised a combined $6.9 million, accounting for only 6.6% of the capital deployed.
For early founders, this highlights the difference between the number of funding opportunities and the actual availability of capital.
Seed-stage activity continued, but the bulk of investor money went to businesses that had progressed further along the fundraising cycle.
Late-stage funding, meanwhile, was entirely driven by Finnable’s Series C transaction. The $43.8 million investment accounted for 42% of the weekly total, illustrating how one sizeable growth-stage deal can significantly influence India’s weekly funding numbers.
Emerging Key Destinations: Fintech, Aerospace and AI
Beyond the overall numbers, the sectoral spread of the investments offers a glimpse into the different technology and business opportunities attracting capital.
Fintech remained prominent, with two significant transactions. Finnable raised $43.8 million in a Series C round, while Mumbai-based Vegapay secured $10 million in Series A funding.
The two businesses operate at different parts of the financial services ecosystem. Finnable provides instant personal loans and financial management tools, while Vegapay develops B2B technology infrastructure for credit, cards, lending and banking products.
